This land is all I know. My parents grew wheat and corn here, and so did their parents. In Quzhou, the soil is deep and flat — good for crops, but the water is the problem. Every year the well goes a little deeper, and I worry about the cost of pumping. But I have to farm what I can.

I have about 8 mu of contracted land. Every year I do the same rotation: winter wheat from October through June, then summer corn straight after. I don't have extra money or knowledge to try something risky like vegetables or cotton — my neighbor tried cotton a few years back and it was a disaster. Wheat and corn I understand. The government supports the price. The village cooperative buys it directly.

For wheat seeds, I'll buy Jimai 22 from the township supply station — most people here use it and yields are decent. For corn, I always buy hybrid seeds, Zhengdan 958 or whatever hybrid the cooperative recommends this year. Hybrid corn gives more, everyone knows this.

Fertilizer: I apply compound fertilizer as base when I plant, then top-dress urea for both crops. I know some people skip potassium but I put a little in — my plots respond better. Irrigation hurts the pocket but I can't skip the winter water for wheat or it suffers from frost heave. Three times for wheat, twice for corn unless summer rains are good.

Pesticides: I spray herbicide in autumn for the wheat, and check in spring for aphids. For corn I spray once for borer. I don't over-apply — it costs money.

Tillage: rotary before wheat every year. For corn I seed directly into the wheat stubble — saves time and fuel.
